markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **recent-conditioned SASRec with 32-negative candidate cross-entropy** as a controlled extension. Benefits remain hypotheses; 0.5050 describes the supplied earlier baseline.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Users report stale interests displacing current purposes. A causal recent-history residual directly targets this pattern while preserving long-term features.
2. Broad similarity produces weak task/content connections. Directed recent-to-target learning may sharpen connections, but cannot establish compatibility or immediate demand.
3. Electronics has an 8.42% training negative-win rate and 0.210 tenth-percentile margin. These motivate candidate-discrimination experiments without identifying the cause of validation errors.

**Insights from related work**

1. [HGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217), [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf), and [SHAN](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2018/546) already combine recent and persistent preferences. Novelty is a compact adaptation, not gated recency or directionality generally.
2. [Sampled-softmax analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02327) motivates competing negatives; [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) provides a calibration comparator. Candidate CE is not full-catalog likelihood, and unobserved negatives may be relevant.
3. [ICSRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773) supports subsequence-derived intent; [ReZero](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v161/bachlechner21a/bachlechner21a.pdf) supports initially inactive residuals. Neither establishes this proposal’s ranking benefit.

**Framework and candidate assessment**

Directions are temporal representation, candidate discrimination, and candidate-specific evidence. Scores include positive/negative reasons; O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32-negative CE only | 2: established/simple | 6: scalable/limited novelty | 4: competition/no recency | 8: separation/cause uncertain | 3: local change/exclusions |
| **Gated recent residual + CE** | 3: compact adaptation/strong precedent | 7: extensible/extra tuning | 8: recency and transitions/no compatibility labels | 8: candidate competition/unverified HR gain | 5: small branch/coordinated deployment |
| [DIN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978)-inspired candidate attention | 4: targeted adaptation/established mechanism | 7: specific evidence/catalog cost | 8: connections/redundancy unresolved | 6: discrimination/indirect evidence | 7: expressive/chunked scoring |

**Selected algorithm**

Pool the last five causal nonpadding embeddings with exponential weights. Add a projected summary through a prefix-dependent scalar sigmoid gate and zero-initialized residual scalar. Separate projection permits asymmetric associations; fixed decay does not learn relevance. Initially only the scalar receives branch gradients; initialize the projection normally and monitor activation.

Train CE over one target and 32 unique uniform alternatives, excluding padding, target, and complete known training positives inside the user-aware sampler. Preserve tensor-only batches. Fix temperature to one; uncertain simulator judgments never become dislikes.

Predeclare baseline, CE-only, residual-only, and combined variants, each capped at 10,800 charged GPU-seconds. Preserve seeds, splits, routing, paths, and the 200-epoch default. Use identical validation cadence and earliest-checkpoint tie-breaking; select by pinned macro HR@10. Save paired user hits and report stratified bootstrap intervals with their conditional limitations. Update predictor and measured diagnostics together; deployed margins, counts, and exclusions must be explicit. Additional pooling, gate, and gBCE controls require remaining budget.

idea.description: Add a causal recent-history residual to each per-dataset SASRec model and train candidate cross-entropy with 32 unique uniform negatives. At every valid position, exponentially pool the last five observed item embeddings, apply a learned directed projection and a prefix-dependent scalar gate, and multiply the residual by a zero-initialized learned scalar. Treat this as a modest combination of established mechanisms, tested through a four-variant factorial comparison.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: older interests overpowering recent activity, and broad historical similarity admitting items without a specific current task or content connection. Recent conditioning addresses the former; projected recent-to-target associations provide a testable mechanism for the latter, without establishing actual usefulness. Candidate competition targets the model-facing Electronics weakness: 8.42% negative-win rate, 0.210 tenth-percentile margin, and 12.47% margins below 0.5 on observed neural training pairs. These associations do not establish causal explanations, validation gains, compatibility, complementarity, immediate demand, or dislike. Electronics embedding alignment of approximately 0.677 is a descriptive diagnostic, not evidence of poor recommendation diversity.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl, their dataset routing, unchanged benchmark splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Do not access hidden test labels, fetch data or pretrained weights, or modify the evaluator. Only histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are available; ignore the contradictory generic metadata example listing unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices and stores.

Use the original SASRec backbone, optimizer, batching and learning-rate schedule unchanged across the initial four variants. Before execution, serialize the inherited concrete settings and all new settings into each trial configuration. Define recent weights as exp(-j), where j=0 denotes the current observed item, over at most five nonpadding observations. Normalize over valid observations; return zero for an empty prefix. The source item at position t is observed and may enter its own next-item prediction; the target at t+1 must never enter the prefix. Set W to a normally initialized bias-free d-by-d linear map. Set G to a scalar affine map of concat(h,r,h-r), initialize its bias to zero and weights with a standard small random initialization, and set scalar a=0. Use z=h+tanh(a)*sigmoid(G(...))*W(r). With a=0, z=h and gradients into W and G through the residual are zero; a generally receives a gradient immediately. Do not also zero W. Monitor a, effective gate magnitude, residual-to-backbone norm ratio, and gradient norms. Identity initialization of this addition does not establish whole-model dynamical isometry.

Implement extra negative sampling inside the existing user-aware sampler before user IDs are discarded. Preserve downstream batches (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L; preserve the original negative tensor and expose additional sampled negatives through a separately indexed training-side payload synchronized with the batch, or use a training-only collate wrapper that consumes user IDs internally before yielding the required batch. Do not infer user identity from truncated histories. Sample 32 unique items uniformly without replacement from IDs 1..N excluding the target and the user's complete training-history set. Never inspect held-out interactions for exclusions. For fewer than 32 eligible items, sample all eligible items and mask remaining slots; skip CE positions with no eligible alternatives and count them. Vectorize rejection sampling and use an explicit eligible-pool fallback for dense users. Record pool sizes M and actual counts k; conditional inclusion probability is k/M. For the CE-only and combined variants, use the identical sampler algorithm and seeded streams, while recognizing that training trajectories differ. False negatives remain possible.

Use unnormalized dot-product logits and temperature tau=1 initially. Optimize the mean valid-position CE over the positive and its sampled alternatives. This is a 33-candidate discrimination objective, not an unbiased full-softmax likelihood. Do not silently multiply by M/32 or add importance corrections: those define another objective, and even a partition estimate followed by a logarithm remains biased at finite sample size. Exclusions change support. Keep the baseline's original BCE and negative count in the baseline and residual-only cells, and label their comparison with CE as a combined objective-and-negative-count intervention. An equal-32-negative BCE/gBCE/CE comparison would isolate objectives, but is a deferred experiment requiring budget. gBCE uses independent sigmoid terms with its published beta correction, not temperature scaling; log its sampling assumptions and normalization if implemented.

Predeclare baseline, CE-only, residual-only, and combined variants. Each receives at most 10,800 charged GPU-seconds across all four categories, training, diagnostics, validation, debugging and failures; all trials together remain within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Use one GPU per trial; concurrent slots do not increase the total budget. Keep the 200-epoch environment default. Evaluate every 10 completed epochs, use no early-stopping patience in this initial comparison, and stop at the shared epoch limit or variant budget cap. Reserve time within each cap for validation and required diagnostics. A macro checkpoint consists of four category checkpoints at the same evaluation milestone; select the largest measured pinned macro validation HR@10, breaking ties by earliest milestone. Record the actual category epochs and steps, and report incomplete milestones or budget truncation rather than inventing scores. Use the same pinned 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42 for every variant. Never substitute a local evaluator for the host's pinned selection metric.

Save each validation user's binary hit with category and stable user identifier when the evaluator exposes it; otherwise mark paired inference unavailable rather than fabricate hits or change the evaluator. Using available hits, estimate pairwise macro differences with 10,000 category-stratified paired bootstrap replicates, seed 42, resampling 200 users independently within each category with shared indices across variants. Report percentile 95% intervals and discordant win/loss counts. Intervals condition on checkpoint selection, seed and candidate sets, excluding selection optimism and training variability. If significance is claimed across multiple comparisons, use separately valid paired tests with a declared multiplicity correction such as Holm; bootstrap intervals alone are not adjusted significance tests. Limit conclusions to the pinned sampled-candidate metric, which may disagree with full-catalog ranking. Record per-category and macro HR@10, checkpoint epoch/step, hardware, training/evaluation/diagnostic time, charged GPU-seconds and wall time.

Serialize architecture settings, source/output embedding conventions, pooling decay, gate, projection, scalar, weights and category routing. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py constructs the exact trained architecture. Reuse fused features and identical dot-product scoring in training and inference. Produce the native full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five/category, without inferring unobserved simulator traits. This candidate-independent branch needs no candidate-specific history attention; chunk catalog matrix multiplication if necessary.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module; preserve item_emb, user_train, meta_data and review_data accessors. Expose fused deployed features through log2feats and their matching dot-product scores through predict_score. Label changed neural-margin semantics explicitly: fused margins are not the previous backbone-only margins. If there is a separate deployed scoring wrapper, probe it directly; otherwise state that neural and deployed scores coincide. Report finite observation counts, exclusions, unique sampled items and sampled embedding counts; keep unavailable category breakdowns unavailable. Null deployed metrics in the supplied diagnosis are missing evidence, not zero error. The interpreter prompt must use actual measured values and definitions and avoid causal or user-trait claims.

Do not expand the initial search to all suggested controls. If budget remains, prioritize last-item versus uniform-last-five versus exponential-last-five pooling, then a scale-matched global scalar versus learned gate or identity versus learned W. A global fixed coefficient must be tuned under the same budget to avoid attributing a scale benefit to adaptive gating. Symmetric W and separate source/target factors can probe directionality, but are deferred. Broader window, decay, temperature, loss and gate sweeps risk validation overfitting on only 800 users. Log every attempted configuration and failure; simulator feedback supplies hypotheses, never training preference labels. No improvement is claimed before measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare four variants: original SASRec; CE-only; residual-only; residual+CE.
Freeze common preprocessing/training seeds, backbone settings, validation cadence and budget policy.
For each variant, cap all four categories and diagnostics at 10,800 charged GPU-seconds:
    For each unchanged category dataset:
        Initialize SASRec; for residual variants initialize W normally, gate G, and a=0.
        In the user-aware sampler, retain complete training-positive exclusion sets.
        Generate required tensor batches; prepare additional negatives before discarding user IDs.
        For every valid causal training position t:
            h_t = SASRec(sequence)[t]
            If residual enabled:
                recent = last at most five observed nonpadding embeddings through t
                r_t = sum_j exp(-j)*recent[j] / sum_j exp(-j)
                g_t = sigmoid(G(concat(h_t, r_t, h_t-r_t)))
                z_t = h_t + tanh(a)*g_t*W(r_t)
            Else: z_t = h_t
            If CE enabled:
                eligible = catalog minus padding, target, complete known training positives
                negatives = uniform_without_replacement(eligible, min(32, len(eligible)))
                If no negatives: count exclusion and skip this CE position
                logits = dot(z_t, output_item_embeddings([target] + negatives))
                loss_t = cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0), tau=1
            Else:
                loss_t = original masked SASRec BCE using its original negative count
        Optimize mean valid-position loss with unchanged baseline optimizer settings.
        Save exact architecture configuration, model weights and training accounting.
    At each common completed 10-epoch milestone within the budget:
        Obtain pinned validation hits and four-category macro HR@10.
        Save the four-model checkpoint bundle.
    Select best complete macro checkpoint bundle; earliest milestone wins ties.
    Generate working/predict.py using matching fused features, dot-product scoring and routing.
    Run compatible diagnostics on actual trained models and record counts and definitions.
    Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five training users/category.
Compare variants using measured macro HR@10, category results and charged GPU time.
Where paired hits are available, compute stratified paired bootstrap intervals and discordant counts.
Report missing evaluations explicitly; never infer hidden test performance.

originality.positive: The initially inactive residual offers a compact, falsifiable SASRec adaptation combining recent conditioning with candidate competition.
originality.negative: HGN, FPMC and SHAN substantially precede gated short-term preference modeling and directed transitions; ReZero precedes zero-initialized residual scaling. Novelty is chiefly the implementation and controlled combination.

future_potential.positive: A small causal branch provides a practical basis for separating recency, transition modeling and candidate competition across four domains, with clear deployment and diagnostic contracts.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, additional controls consume a limited budget, and histories alone cannot resolve compatibility, redundancy or immediate demand. Repeated selection on the same small validation cohort risks optimism.

code_difficulty.positive: The representation branch is small and retains candidate-independent scoring and the SASRec backbone.
code_difficulty.negative: User-aware negative exclusion, synchronized tensor-only batches, coordinated category checkpoint selection, budget enforcement, predictor generation and diagnostic consistency make the complete experiment moderately complex.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to represent sequential interaction histories.
Provides the existing per-dataset backbone and already models short- and long-range dependencies.
limitations: Does not establish product compatibility or current demand.
Its architecture alone does not demonstrate performance on this pinned evaluation.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax recommendation analysis
contributions: Analyzes emphasis on high-scoring negatives and the role of temperature.
Motivates separate consideration of score normalization during training and inference.
limitations: General recommendation findings require verification in this SASRec benchmark.
Does not establish that easy negatives caused Electronics' observed weakness or that normalization will improve this task.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Combines increased negative sampling with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
Provides a comparator with independent sigmoid terms and a sampling-dependent positive-term correction.
limitations: Does not directly resolve stale-interest dominance or verify item usefulness.
Loss effects must be separated from negative-count effects using matched sampling controls.

related_work.title: Intent Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Learns latent intents from subsequences using contrastive objectives without explicit intent labels.
limitations: Does not establish observed session boundaries or functional compatibility.
Its additional objectives are more involved than the proposed early-stage residual.

related_work.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Uses candidate-conditioned history weighting to model candidate-specific interests.
limitations: Candidate-dependent history scoring increases full-catalog inference cost.
Attention weights do not verify compatibility, complementarity or dislike.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines gated recent-item representations, persistent preferences and direct recent-to-candidate interactions.
Provides substantial precedent for the proposal's pooled short-term and transition mechanisms.
limitations: Its hierarchical gates differ from the proposed single pooled-summary gate.
Mechanistic overlap does not establish comparative performance on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines persistent user preferences with factorized recent-item transitions.
Separate source and target factors permit directional associations.
limitations: Predictive transitions do not identify genuine complementarity or functional compatibility.
Does not establish the incremental value of the proposed SASRec residual.

related_work.title: Sequential Recommender System Based on Hierarchical Attention Networks
contributions: Combines historical preferences and recent demand through hierarchical attention.
limitations: Provides precedent rather than evidence for this specific residual formulation.
Recent interaction evidence does not establish immediate purchasing demand.

related_work.title: ReZero Is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Uses zero-initialized residual scaling to begin from an identity contribution.
Clarifies why residual parameters initially receive no branch gradient while the scalar can activate.
limitations: Does not demonstrate ranking benefits for this recommender.
An identity local addition does not establish whole-model dynamical isometry; activation can stall with unsuitable initialization.

related_work.title: Highway Networks
contributions: Provides precedent for gated transformations and initially favoring a carry path.
limitations: A strongly saturated gate can suppress learning.
Does not justify a particular initialization or accuracy claim for this residual.

related_work.title: Candidate Sampling Reference
contributions: Explains candidate-sampling distributions and correction conventions relevant to sampled objectives.
limitations: Corrections depend on sampling support and probabilities.
Uncorrected candidate CE should not be described as full-catalog likelihood.

related_work.title: Adaptive Sampled Softmax with Kernel Based Sampling
contributions: Analyzes sampled-softmax estimation and the importance of the proposal distribution.
limitations: Finite-sample log-partition estimates can remain biased.
Importance correction cannot recover items assigned zero sampling probability.

related_work.title: gSASRec official implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for generalized BCE and negative-sampling settings.
limitations: Its sampling assumptions and normalization must be checked before adapting the correction.
Implementation availability does not imply gains under this benchmark's exclusions and budget.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling mechanics useful for comparing predictions on identical users.
limitations: Category stratification must be implemented explicitly.
Intervals conditional on selected predictions omit training variability and checkpoint-selection optimism.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled-candidate rankings can disagree with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator.
Supports limiting conclusions to the evaluated candidate protocol.
